column1: # Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (Switch 2): the keys its files decide, plus what the other Nintendo EPD games on NVN2 needed. A first profile: see README.md for what is checked
# main takes nothing from subsdk1 (nn::camera), subsdk2, subsdk3 (C / libc) or subsdk4 (C++) that the host does not supply (profile_guess.py)
# A workaround, cause open: Npc_Integration model heaps come up 65-80 bytes short (README.md)

# The game asks SetHeapSize for 0x1de400000 (7.5 GB) in nninitStartup: a 4 GB alias region and an 8 GB heap region. The alias size is Splatoon Raiders', not measured here. The NPDM declares a 32 MB system resource
# Golf in Handheld: the game's upscaler takes about 4.7 ms a frame, MetalFX about 0.9 ms, about 41 fps against 48 (README.md, Performance)
# Dynamic resolution reads the GPU time between the frame's timestamp reports. With one time per submission it reads about 0 and the game stays at its largest size, well below 60 fps;
# with each report on its segment's GPU start / end, in Handheld with MetalFX, it goes down to mostly 640x360 at about 44 to 60 fps, mostly 52 to 60 (README.md, Performance)
# The game steps its systems by a frame rate its framework picks from the frame's CPU time alone (60 in play), so frames that wait on the GPU played slow on a Mac that cannot
# hold 60. The rate takes the host's frame step instead (FRAME_STEP in patches.py, v65536): 60 fps, 30 or 20 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# Not checked on this game yet: the sead / agl engine of Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders wraps its clears in render conditions
